citation_verdicts.note: A list item among assessment report contents; supports the narrow claim made.
Supports the claim as scoped (oversight of a DMMA); it is not guidance on escalation paths, as the reader's caveat already says.
Also scoped to the DMMA process, not to governance generally.
Describes the centralized model specifically (formal executive position). Used for A-04 Option A as an analogy for a single accountable leader; the quote is not general escalation guidance.
Sentence runs across pages 928-929; the quoted part is on 928.
The same paragraph cautions that an existing committee may not give data management enough attention; Option B in A-04 does say 'cautiously'.
Qualified by 'In many organizations'; the reader's wording keeps this qualification.

The Help Desk Administrator is an IT support role for issues with information systems or infrastructure. Using it to say DMBOK2 keeps incident handling out of the steward role is the reader's own analogy, which the caveat admits. It does not itself separate data-steward work from incident resolution.

row_verdicts.note: Project (README line 44, HANDOFF non-goal line 42) frames a governance role excluding operational incident handling; Chapter 16 7.2.2 frames stewardship as governance, so Aligned holds. The wording action is sensible because DMBOK2 says stewards help identify and resolve data issues. Do not lean on the Help Desk citation (C16-34) as support for the exclusion; it is an analogy.

HANDOFF line 72 and the contract (lines 71, 78) keep ownership assignment with humans and surface gaps. Chapters 15-16 do not define the Data Owner role, so Partial rests on thin evidence; the status could move if the governance-chapter reader finds a fuller Data Owner definition.

agent-risk-reviewer.md confirms the role is unnamed and defaults to the project owner (line 304); no governance body or sponsor exists. Partial with structural-proposal is fair; Missing would be too harsh because an escalation route exists. Options are labelled as proposals.
README line 41 lists governance reporting but no content, cadence or measures are defined; the Success criteria are qualitative. Partial/wording fits.
Project only lists continuous improvement (README line 42). DMBOK2 ties it to baseline and scheduled re-assessment (p898). Partial/wording fits.
HANDOFF line 25 matches stakeholder engagement in intent, but no stakeholders are named and no routing destination exists. Partial/wording is fair.

Status fair: the project defines agent-layer decision rights but no human operating model. Caution on Option A: the single-steward arrangement is not really DMBOK2's decentralized model, which is committee-based with no single owner (p912-913), so calling it 'the current de facto position' is a stretch; the single human steward is closer to the centralized 'one person' pattern at small scale. The proposed options should be worded as proposals only, and a record-deviation remains a valid alternative.

HANDOFF Success criteria (line 293) are qualitative target-state conditions with no scale or baseline, and no maturity measure exists. Partial/structural-proposal is fair, and the record-deviation alternative is noted. Option A's readiness caveat (p877) is correctly stated.

missing_findings.note: Operating-model tips: 'Get executive sponsorship - a must for a sustainable model' and 'Use what already exists'. Directly relevant to the unnamed governance owner and to the choice between a new body and an existing committee; not cited for A-04.

6.1 CDO section: CDO mandates include establishing governance standards, policies and procedures, and a DMO commonly reports through the CDO. Relevant to who the named governance owner could be (Option A). Section 6.2 on p934-935 (Data Governance Office as policy lead, 'highly regulated environments where the emphasis is on policy and accountability') is also relevant and not cited.

7.1: 'Data Stewards are often part of a Data Governance Organization' and such an organisation facilitates bodies such as the Data Governance Council. Bears on where the project's single steward sits; not cited.

Section 6: 'The lifecycle itself should be governed' - a maturity assessment lifecycle (planning, assessment, recommendations, action plan, periodic re-evaluation) needs governance of its own. Relevant to continuous improvement and to A-32 cadence/ownership; not cited.
4.6 Stakeholder Engagement: map stakeholders by influence and interest to choose how to engage them. Supports the stakeholder-register suggestion for A-08; not cited.

6.2 metrics list says spend-management metrics 'overlap with data governance metrics' and lists effectiveness of communication and training, speed of change adoption. Relevant to what governance reporting could cover; not cited.
